title: Dualizing complex of the point
statement:
Use the Poincare duality conventions [def-pod-conventions], with $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $a_s=\operatorname{id}_s$, and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$. On the bounded constructible point category $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], the constructible exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] of the identity is naturally isomorphic to the identity. In particular,
$$
\omega_{s,\Lambda}=Ra_s^!\Lambda_s\cong\Lambda_s.
$$
For every $C\in D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ put $c=\operatorname{Fib}_s(C)$, using the point fibre equivalence [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence], and define $D_sC=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\omega_{s,\Lambda})$ using [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Then there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
\operatorname{Fib}_s(D_sC)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(c,\Lambda)=c^\vee.
$$
Here $c^\vee$ is the derived coefficient-module dual of [def-pod-perfect-point-complex]. At finite and integral coefficients the evaluation on the left means termwise sections $\Gamma(s,-)$ on the ambient derived category, as in [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]; at $E$ it means its rationalization, and at $\Qlb$ it means its common finite-stage version. Thus this formula spells out $D_sC\cong C^\vee$ under the point-category identifications, rather than identifying a sheaf complex with a coefficient-module complex without evaluation.

proof.text: The identity compactification and [lem-pod-identity-compact-support-normalization] give a specified natural isomorphism $Ra_{s!}\cong\operatorname{id}$ at all four coefficient stages, with the integral normalization and common-stage compatibilities fixed by that lemma.

source.place: first sentence: identity compact support and uniqueness of its constructible right adjoint

proof.text: Use the constructible adjunction $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ of [def-pod-conventions, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], which that definition records as a theorem rather than a part of the definition; for $f=a_s$ it is supplied stage by stage as follows. At $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, take the compactification $c=(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id})$ with $\dim s=0$ in [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], clause 2: there $P_c=Ra_{s!,n}$ and $R_c=\nu_s^*a_s^{\times}R\nu_{s,*}=Ra^!_{s,n}$, and every $K\in D^b_c(s,A_{E,n})$ has an etale-origin witness by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] (ii), so $\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_{s!}K,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,Ra_s^!L)$ naturally for $K,L\in D^b_c(s,A_{E,n})$, the categories being full. At $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, the separated finite-type morphism $a_s$ of [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint] gives $G_{a_s}$, with the object formula $R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRa^!_{s,n}L_n$ of the integral exceptional functor, right adjoint to integral $Ra_{s!}$ on $D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$. At $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$ the finite-Tor categories are by definition the bounded constructible ones, and [lem-sf-constructible-exceptional-adjunction-coefficients] gives the natural adjunction $Ra_{s!,\Lambda}\dashv Ra^!_{s,\Lambda}$ on them. For any $K,L$ in that category, its natural Hom bijection becomes $\operatorname{Hom}(K,Ra_s^!L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,L)$. Write the resulting natural bijection as $\Phi_K:\operatorname{Hom}(K,Ra_s^!L)\to\operatorname{Hom}(K,L)$. Set $u=\Phi_{Ra_s^!L}(1)$ and $v=\Phi_L^{-1}(1)$. Naturality in $K$ gives $uv=1$ and $\Phi_{Ra_s^!L}(vu)=u=\Phi_{Ra_s^!L}(1)$, hence $vu=1$ by injectivity. Thus $u$ is an isomorphism; naturality of the original bijections in $L$ makes it a natural isomorphism. At $L=\Lambda_s$ it gives $\omega_{s,\Lambda}\cong\Lambda_s$. This concerns the constructible adjoint, not the comparison composite on arbitrary pro-etale complexes.

source.place: first sentence: identity compact support and uniqueness of its constructible right adjoint

proof.text: The coefficient DVR theorem [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] applies; its principal-ideal property makes $\mathcal O_E$ and its quotients Noetherian. For the finite and integral cases write $(R,B)=(A_{E,n},(A_{E,n})_s)$ or $(\mathcal O_E,\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s})$. Let $\underline M$ be the constant sheaf and set $L_R(M)=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M$. Exact sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] makes the constant module functor exact; at finite level $L_R(M)=\underline M$, and at integral level flatness of $B$ over $\underline R$ [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] makes $L_R$ exact. Sections $\Gamma(s,-)$ are exact by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. The continuous-coefficient description [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction] gives $\Gamma(s,\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s})=C(\{*\},\mathcal O_E)=\mathcal O_E$. The reduction theorem identifies $B/\varpi_E^n B$ with $(A_{E,n})_s$; multiplication by $\varpi_E^n$ is injective on $B$, since $\mathcal O_E$ is a domain and $B$ is flat. Exact sections therefore identify $\Gamma(s,(A_{E,n})_s)=A_{E,n}$, through the canonical constant-value map. Thus in both cases $\Gamma(s,B)=R$. There is an explicit adjunction $L_R\dashv\Gamma(s,-)$: a map $v:L_RM\to F$ gives $m\mapsto v_s(1\otimes m)$; a linear map $t:M\to F(s)$ gives $b\otimes m\mapsto b\,t(m)|_U$ on every object $U$. Balancing and sheafification make the latter a sheaf map. The formulas are inverse and natural, and their termwise versions commute with the complex differentials.

Apply [lem-pod-point-sections-reconstruction] to the exact adjunction of step 3 and its equality $\Gamma(s,B)=R$. With $c=\Gamma(s,C)$ it supplies the actual counit $L_Rc\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ in $D^b_c(s,R)$, and integrally a bounded finite-projective model $P$ of $c$. The bounded finite/finitely generated cohomology of $c$ is part of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Thus replacing $C$ by $L_Rc$ uses this specified counit and does not identify arbitrary pro-etale sheaves with modules.

source.place: second sentence, with its point-category identification made explicit

proof.text: Choose a K-injective resolution $B\to I$ for [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The complex $\Gamma(s,I)$ is K-injective over $R$: if $Q$ is acyclic, exactness of $L_R$ makes $L_RQ$ acyclic, and the termwise adjunction identifies a map $Q\to\Gamma(s,I)$ with a map $L_RQ\to I$, homotopic to zero by [def-pur-kinjective-complex]; the adjunction sends that homotopy back to a homotopy. Exact sections make $R=\Gamma(s,B)\to\Gamma(s,I)$ a quasi-isomorphism. Thus $\Gamma(s,I)$ is a K-injective resolution of $R$.

source.place: K-injective Hom-complex construction preceding Tag 0A94, lemma-RHom-into-K-injective; exact-left-adjoint argument written explicitly

proof.text: Represent $c$ by a coefficient-module complex and $C$ by $L_Rc$ using step 4. The derived internal Hom is represented by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet_B(L_Rc,I)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Its sections have terms $\prod_p\operatorname{Hom}_B(L_Rc^p,I^{p+j})=\prod_p\operatorname{Hom}_R(c^p,\Gamma(s,I^{p+j}))$ by the adjunction of step 3. Naturality makes the differentials on both sides $d_I\circ f-(-1)^j f\circ d_c$, as in [def-pur-hom-complex]. Therefore these are isomorphic as complexes, not merely as their cohomology groups. Step 5 identifies the right complex with a representative of $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(c,R)$. Together with steps 1–2 this gives $\Gamma(s,D_sC)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(c,R)=c^\vee$ [def-pod-perfect-point-complex], naturally in $C$, at finite and integral coefficients. No finite projective representative of $c$ was required in this computation at finite level. At integral level, use the bounded finite-projective model $P$ from step 4. Termwise sheaf Hom from $L_RP^i$ is a direct summand of a finite power of the identity functor, hence exact. The finite total Hom complex therefore sends an acyclic second input to an acyclic complex: filter by the finitely many degrees of $P$, whose successive quotients are shifted exact Hom complexes. Consequently $\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(L_RP,B)\to\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(L_RP,I)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Its source is $L_R(\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,R))$, a bounded finite-projective model, so [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] puts the internal Hom itself in $D^b_c(s,R)$. This verifies the domain required for its rationalization in step 7.

source.place: Tag 0A94, lemma-RHom-into-K-injective, and the Hom-complex definition; adjunction identifies every term and differential

proof.text: At the rational stage represent $C_E$ by an integral object $C$ as prescribed by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Step 4 supplies a bounded finite-projective $R=\mathcal O_E$ complex $P$ representing $c=\Gamma(s,C)$. Rationalizing the isomorphism of step 6 gives $\Gamma(s,R\mathcal Hom_R(C,B))\otimes_R E\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,R)\otimes_R E\cong\operatorname{Hom}_E^\bullet(P\otimes_R E,E)$; the last isomorphism is [lem-pc-base-change-rhom-perfect]. This is the required $E$-coefficient formula, including inputs whose chosen integral representatives have torsion. An arrow $u\otimes a$ acts on the dual by precomposition with $u$ and multiplication by $a$ on both sides, so naturality holds on the localized morphisms. For algebraically closed coefficients represent $C$ by $(E,C_E)$ and compute the unit and internal Hom at that same finite field, as in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The displayed isomorphism then defines the claimed arrow at stage $E$. To check independence of stage, choose a common finite extension $L$ for any input arrow. The fibre scalar comparison [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] identifies its coefficient complex with $c_E\otimes_E L$. Apply [lem-pod-point-scalar-hom-evaluation] to $P$ and its dual model from step 6. It identifies the actual internal-Hom scalar comparison, through the specified completed and point-sections comparisons, with the coefficient scalar-Hom arrow, naturally in $P$ and compatibly with $E\subset L\subset M$. Thus extending the finite-stage duality arrow preserves that arrow, and an input morphism represented over $L$ has its naturality square there. The coherent diagrams make the resulting common-stage arrow independent of all representatives. This gives the required $\Qlb$ formula with the specified coefficient comparisons.
